paragraphs.text: And he entered again into the synagogue; and there was a man there who had his hand withered.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ εἰσῆλθεν πάλιν εἰς συναγωγήν, καὶ ἦν ἐκεῖ ἄνθρωπος ἐξηραμμένην ἔχων τὴν χεῖρα.
paragraphs.translit: Kai eisēlthen palin eis synagōgēn, kai ēn ekei anthrōpos exērammenēn echōn tēn cheira.

paragraphs.text: And they watched him, whether he would heal him on the sabbath day; that they might accuse him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ παρετήρουν αὐτὸν εἰ τοῖς σάββασιν θεραπεύσει αὐτόν, ἵνα κατηγορήσωσιν αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai paretēroun auton ei tois sabbasin therapeusei auton, hina katēgorēsōsin autou.

paragraphs.text: And he saith unto the man that had his hand withered, Stand forth.
paragraphs.original: καὶ λέγει τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τῷ τὴν χεῖρα ἔχοντι ξηράν· Ἔγειρε εἰς τὸ μέσον.
paragraphs.translit: kai legei tō anthrōpō tō tēn cheira echonti xēran· Egeire eis to meson.

paragraphs.text: And he saith unto them, Is it lawful on the sabbath day to do good, or to do harm? to save a life, or to kill? But they held their peace.
paragraphs.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἔξεστιν τοῖς σάββασιν ἀγαθοποιῆσαι ἢ κακοποιῆσαι, ψυχὴν σῶσαι ἢ ἀποκτεῖναι; οἱ δὲ ἐσιώπων.
paragraphs.translit: kai legei autois· Exestin tois sabbasin agathopoiēsai ē kakopoiēsai, psychēn sōsai ē apokteinai; hoi de esiōpōn.

paragraphs.text: And when he had looked round about on them with anger, being grieved at the hardening of their heart, he saith unto the man, Stretch forth thy hand. And he stretched it forth; and his hand was restored.
paragraphs.original: καὶ περιβλεψάμενος αὐτοὺς μετʼ ὀργῆς, συλλυπούμενος ἐπὶ τῇ πωρώσει τῆς καρδίας αὐτῶν, λέγει τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ· Ἔκτεινον τὴν χεῖρα· καὶ ἐξέτεινεν, καὶ ἀπεκατεστάθη ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai periblepsamenos autous metʼ orgēs, syllypoumenos epi tē pōrōsei tēs kardias autōn, legei tō anthrōpō· Ekteinon tēn cheira· kai exeteinen, kai apekatestathē hē cheir autou.

paragraphs.text: And the Pharisees went out, and straightway with the Herodians took counsel against him, how they might destroy him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐξελθόντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι εὐθὺς μετὰ τῶν Ἡρῳδιανῶν συμβούλιον ἐδίδουν κατʼ αὐτοῦ ὅπως αὐτὸν ἀπολέσωσιν.
paragraphs.translit: kai exelthontes hoi Pharisaioi euthys meta tōn Hērōdianōn symboulion edidoun katʼ autou hopōs auton apolesōsin.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus with his disciples withdrew to the sea: and a great multitude from Galilee followed; and from Judaea,
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ἀνεχώρησεν πρὸς τὴν θάλασσαν· καὶ πολὺ πλῆθος ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἠκολούθησεν, καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας
paragraphs.translit: Kai ho Iēsous meta tōn mathētōn autou anechōrēsen pros tēn thalassan· kai poly plēthos apo tēs Galilaias ēkolouthēsen, kai apo tēs Ioudaias

paragraphs.text: and from Jerusalem, and from Idumaea, and beyond the Jordan, and about Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, hearing what great things he did, came unto him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰδουμαίας καὶ πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου καὶ περὶ Τύρον καὶ Σιδῶνα, πλῆθος πολύ, ἀκούοντες ὅσα ἐποίει ἦλθον πρὸς αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: kai apo Hierosolymōn kai apo tēs Idoumaias kai peran tou Iordanou kai peri Tyron kai Sidōna, plēthos poly, akouontes hosa epoiei ēlthon pros auton.

paragraphs.text: And he spake to his disciples, that a little boat should wait on him because of the crowd, lest they should throng him:
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ἵνα πλοιάριον προσκαρτερῇ αὐτῷ διὰ τὸν ὄχλον ἵνα μὴ θλίβωσιν αὐτόν·
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen tois mathētais autou hina ploiarion proskarterē autō dia ton ochlon hina mē thlibōsin auton·

paragraphs.text: for he had healed many; insomuch that as many as had plagues pressed upon him that they might touch him.
paragraphs.original: πολλοὺς γὰρ ἐθεράπευσεν, ὥστε ἐπιπίπτειν αὐτῷ ἵνα αὐτοῦ ἅψωνται ὅσοι εἶχον μάστιγας.
paragraphs.translit: pollous gar etherapeusen, hōste epipiptein autō hina autou hapsōntai hosoi eichon mastigas.

paragraphs.text: And the unclean spirits, whensoever they beheld him, fell down before him, and cried, saying, Thou art the Son of God.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἀκάθαρτα, ὅταν αὐτὸν ἐθεώρουν, προσέπιπτον αὐτῷ καὶ ἔκραζον λέγοντα ὅτι Σὺ εἶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai ta pneumata ta akatharta, hotan auton etheōroun, prosepipton autō kai ekrazon legonta hoti Sy ei ho hyios tou theou.

paragraphs.text: And he charged them much that they should not make him known.
paragraphs.original: καὶ πολλὰ ἐπετίμα αὐτοῖς ἵνα μὴ αὐτὸν φανερὸν ποιήσωσιν.
paragraphs.translit: kai polla epetima autois hina mē auton phaneron poiēsōsin.

paragraphs.text: And he goeth up into the mountain, and calleth unto him whom he himself would; and they went unto him.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἀναβαίνει εἰς τὸ ὄρος καὶ προσκαλεῖται οὓς ἤθελεν αὐτός, καὶ ἀπῆλθον πρὸς αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai anabainei eis to oros kai proskaleitai hous ēthelen autos, kai apēlthon pros auton.

paragraphs.text: And he appointed twelve, that they might be with him, and that he might send them forth to preach,
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐποίησεν δώδεκα, ἵνα ὦσιν μετʼ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἵνα ἀποστέλλῃ αὐτοὺς κηρύσσειν
paragraphs.translit: kai epoiēsen dōdeka, hina ōsin metʼ autou kai hina apostellē autous kēryssein

paragraphs.text: and to have authority to cast out demons:
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔχειν ἐξουσίαν ἐκβάλλειν τὰ δαιμόνια·
paragraphs.translit: kai echein exousian ekballein ta daimonia·

paragraphs.text: and Simon he surnamed Peter;
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐποίησεν τοὺς δώδεκα, καὶ ἐπέθηκεν ὄνομα τῷ Σίμωνι Πέτρον,
paragraphs.translit: kai epoiēsen tous dōdeka, kai epethēken onoma tō Simōni Petron,

paragraphs.text: and James the [son] of Zebedee, and John the brother of James; and them he surnamed Boanerges, which is, Sons of thunder:
paragraphs.original: καὶ Ἰάκωβον τὸν τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ Ἰωάννην τὸν ἀδελφὸν τοῦ Ἰακώβου (καὶ ἐπέθηκεν αὐτοῖς ὀνόματα Βοανηργές, ὅ ἐστιν Υἱοὶ Βροντῆς),
paragraphs.translit: kai Iakōbon ton tou Zebedaiou kai Iōannēn ton adelphon tou Iakōbou (kai epethēken autois onomata Boanērges, ho estin Hyioi Brontēs),

paragraphs.text: and Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the [son] of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Cananaean,
paragraphs.original: καὶ Ἀνδρέαν καὶ Φίλιππον καὶ Βαρθολομαῖον καὶ Μαθθαῖον καὶ Θωμᾶν καὶ Ἰάκωβον τὸν τοῦ Ἁλφαίου καὶ Θαδδαῖον καὶ Σίμωνα τὸν Καναναῖον
paragraphs.translit: kai Andrean kai Philippon kai Bartholomaion kai Maththaion kai Thōman kai Iakōbon ton tou Halphaiou kai Thaddaion kai Simōna ton Kananaion

paragraphs.text: and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him. And he cometh into a house.
paragraphs.original: καὶ Ἰούδαν Ἰσκαριώθ, ὃς καὶ παρέδωκεν αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: kai Ioudan Iskariōth, hos kai paredōken auton.

paragraphs.text: And the multitude cometh together again, so that they could not so much as eat bread.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἔρχεται εἰς οἶκον· καὶ συνέρχεται πάλιν ὁ ὄχλος, ὥστε μὴ δύνασθαι αὐτοὺς μηδὲ ἄρτον φαγεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai erchetai eis oikon· kai synerchetai palin ho ochlos, hōste mē dynasthai autous mēde arton phagein.

paragraphs.text: And when his friends heard it, they went out to lay hold on him: for they said, He is beside himself.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ παρʼ αὐτοῦ ἐξῆλθον κρατῆσαι αὐτόν, ἔλεγον γὰρ ὅτι ἐξέστη.
paragraphs.translit: kai akousantes hoi parʼ autou exēlthon kratēsai auton, elegon gar hoti exestē.

paragraphs.text: And the scribes that came down from Jerusalem said, He hath Beelzebub, and, By the prince of the demons casteth he out the demons.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς οἱ ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων καταβάντες ἔλεγον ὅτι Βεελζεβοὺλ ἔχει καὶ ὅτι ἐν τῷ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια.
paragraphs.translit: kai hoi grammateis hoi apo Hierosolymōn katabantes elegon hoti Beelzeboul echei kai hoti en tō archonti tōn daimoniōn ekballei ta daimonia.

paragraphs.text: And he called them unto him, and said unto them in parables, How can Satan cast out Satan?
paragraphs.original: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος αὐτοὺς ἐν παραβολαῖς ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Πῶς δύναται Σατανᾶς Σατανᾶν ἐκβάλλειν;
paragraphs.translit: kai proskalesamenos autous en parabolais elegen autois· Pōs dynatai Satanas Satanan ekballein;

paragraphs.text: And if a kingdom be divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐὰν βασιλεία ἐφʼ ἑαυτὴν μερισθῇ, οὐ δύναται σταθῆναι ἡ βασιλεία ἐκείνη·
paragraphs.translit: kai ean basileia ephʼ heautēn meristhē, ou dynatai stathēnai hē basileia ekeinē·

paragraphs.text: And if a house be divided against itself, that house will not be able to stand.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐὰν οἰκία ἐφʼ ἑαυτὴν μερισθῇ, οὐ δυνήσεται ἡ οἰκία ἐκείνη σταθῆναι·
paragraphs.translit: kai ean oikia ephʼ heautēn meristhē, ou dynēsetai hē oikia ekeinē stathēnai·

paragraphs.text: And if Satan hath rise up against himself, and is divided, he cannot stand, but hath an end.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἰ ὁ Σατανᾶς ἀνέστη ἐφʼ ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἐμερίσθη, οὐ δύναται στῆναι ἀλλὰ τέλος ἔχει.
paragraphs.translit: kai ei ho Satanas anestē ephʼ heauton kai emeristhē, ou dynatai stēnai alla telos echei.

paragraphs.text: But no one can enter into the house of the strong [man], and spoil his goods, except he first bind the strong [man]; and then he will spoil his house.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλʼ οὐδεὶς δύναται εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν τοῦ ἰσχυροῦ εἰσελθὼν τὰ σκεύη αὐτοῦ διαρπάσαι ἐὰν μὴ πρῶτον τὸν ἰσχυρὸν δήσῃ, καὶ τότε τὴν οἰκίαν αὐτοῦ διαρπάσει.
paragraphs.translit: allʼ oudeis dynatai eis tēn oikian tou ischyrou eiselthōn ta skeuē autou diarpasai ean mē prōton ton ischyron dēsē, kai tote tēn oikian autou diarpasei.

paragraphs.text: Verily I say unto you, All their sins shall be forgiven unto the sons of men, and their blasphemies wherewith soever they shall blaspheme:
paragraphs.original: Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πάντα ἀφεθήσεται τοῖς υἱοῖς τῶν ἀνθρώπων, τὰ ἁμαρτήματα καὶ αἱ βλασφημίαι ὅσα ἐὰν βλασφημήσωσιν·
paragraphs.translit: Amēn legō hymin hoti panta aphethēsetai tois hyiois tōn anthrōpōn, ta hamartēmata kai hai blasphēmiai hosa ean blasphēmēsōsin·

paragraphs.text: but whosoever shall blaspheme against the Holy Spirit hath never forgiveness, but is guilty of an eternal sin:
paragraphs.original: ὃς δʼ ἂν βλασφημήσῃ εἰς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, οὐκ ἔχει ἄφεσιν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, ἀλλὰ ἔνοχός ἐστιν αἰωνίου ἁμαρτήματος.
paragraphs.translit: hos dʼ an blasphēmēsē eis to pneuma to hagion, ouk echei aphesin eis ton aiōna, alla enochos estin aiōniou hamartēmatos.

paragraphs.text: because they said, He hath an unclean spirit.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι ἔλεγον· Πνεῦμα ἀκάθαρτον ἔχει.
paragraphs.translit: hoti elegon· Pneuma akatharton echei.

paragraphs.text: And there come his mother and his brethren; and, standing without, they sent unto him, calling him.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἔρχονται ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔξω στήκοντες ἀπέστειλαν πρὸς αὐτὸν καλοῦντες αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai erchontai hē mētēr autou kai hoi adelphoi autou kai exō stēkontes apesteilan pros auton kalountes auton.

paragraphs.text: And a multitude was sitting about him; and they say unto him, Behold, thy mother and thy brethren without seek for thee.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐκάθητο περὶ αὐτὸν ὄχλος, καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Ἰδοὺ ἡ μήτηρ σου καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί σου ἔξω ζητοῦσίν σε.
paragraphs.translit: kai ekathēto peri auton ochlos, kai legousin autō· Idou hē mētēr sou kai hoi adelphoi sou exō zētousin se.

paragraphs.text: And he answereth them, and saith, Who is my mother and my brethren?
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτοῖς λέγει· Τίς ἐστιν ἡ μήτηρ μου ἢ οἱ ἀδελφοί μου;
paragraphs.translit: kai apokritheis autois legei· Tis estin hē mētēr mou ē hoi adelphoi mou;

paragraphs.text: And looking round on them that sat round about him, he saith, Behold, my mother and my brethren!
paragraphs.original: καὶ περιβλεψάμενος τοὺς περὶ αὐτὸν κύκλῳ καθημένους λέγει· Ἴδε ἡ μήτηρ μου καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί μου·
paragraphs.translit: kai periblepsamenos tous peri auton kyklō kathēmenous legei· Ide hē mētēr mou kai hoi adelphoi mou·

paragraphs.text: For whosoever shall do the will of God, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.
paragraphs.original: ὃς γὰρ ἂν ποιήσῃ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ, οὗτος ἀδελφός μου καὶ ἀδελφὴ καὶ μήτηρ ἐστίν.
paragraphs.translit: hos gar an poiēsē to thelēma tou theou, houtos adelphos mou kai adelphē kai mētēr estin.
